About us

Relay is a cross-chain payments protocol that provides instant, low-cost cross-chain bridging, swaps, and transactions. We're the fastest and cheapest way to bridge and transact across chains, serving over 5 million users who have completed 59+ million transactions with $6+ billion in volume across 85+ chains.

Our company mission is to make transacting across chains as fast, cheap, and reliable as online payments. We are building the core infrastructure to abstract chains from end user payments, enabling the next billion users to experience the benefits of blockchain without the UX burdens.

About the role

The Liquidity team keeps Relay's liquidity reliable, competitively priced, capital-efficient, and within its risk framework. Behind that are the systems that hold and move Relay's inventory across chains, wallets, exchanges and bridges: rebalancing, targets and limits, route pricing, venue and bridge integrations, and monitoring. They grew quickly with our partner deals. The next phase adds a ledger and P&L, reference data, a risk engine, a rebalance state machine, dynamic fees and a liquidity layer for protocol-level liquidity.

As Principal Engineer, Liquidity, you will own the architecture across these systems: the target design, the build order and the key technical decisions. You will work with the Head of Liquidity, with the team's tech lead, who leads day-to-day delivery, and with our quant developers, who build the pricing, hedging and rebalancing models. You will stay hands-on: prototyping, writing code on the critical paths and reviewing high-risk changes.

We work agentic-first: AI agents extend how much we can design, build and verify, while people remain accountable for decisions that move capital.

What you'll do

Own the liquidity architecture

  • Define the target architecture and build order across rebalancing, pricing and fees, limits and risk, ledger and P&L, reference data, and venue and bridge integrations.

  • Make build-versus-reuse and technology choices, and write down the trade-offs.

  • Set reliability standards for systems that move funds: idempotent operations, explicit state machines, reconciliation, observability, kill switches and safe rollouts.

  • Set latency budgets for the liquidity inputs on the fill path (pricing, limits and inventory used by our solver), and keep slower work, such as ledger writes, off that path.

Design new systems with the engineers who build them

  • Write and review designs for the ledger and P&L, reference data, the risk engine, the rebalance state machine and dynamic pricing.

  • Turn quant models into production designs with the quant developers.

  • Write code on the critical paths and review high-risk changes.

Design the liquidity layer

  • Design protocol-level liquidity and the liquidity layer with our Protocol team.

  • Define Liquidity's requirements and components for Relay's next-generation core.

  • Design how liquidity systems run on separate infrastructure, with their own keys, access and controls.

Raise the engineering bar

  • Run design reviews and mentor senior engineers.

  • Replace one-off partner setup with configuration and shared tooling, so new partners and chains go live without code changes.

  • Help hire the engineers who will build these systems.

About you

  • You've owned the architecture of systems where a bug costs money, and you design for failure first.

  • You design for speed as well as correctness: you know where the time goes on a request path and keep slow work off it.

  • You write clear design documents and bring a team to agreement without being its manager.

  • You stay hands-on: you prototype, write code on the hard paths and review.

  • You choose the simplest design that will hold for the next few years, and you sequence the work so value ships early.

  • You use AI agents to explore designs, write and test code and check your reasoning, and you validate what they produce.

  • You're excited about crypto and the engineering problems of cross-chain liquidity.

Skills and abilities

Must-have

  • 10+ years building backend or distributed systems, including several years as a staff or principal engineer or architect owning architecture across multiple systems.

  • Experience building and operating systems with real-money consequences: trading, exchange, payments, treasury, ledger or market-making systems.

  • Deep knowledge of correctness in financial systems: ledgers and double-entry accounting, idempotency, state machines, reconciliation and partial failures across external systems.

  • Experience designing and running systems with tight latency budgets on the request path (single-digit milliseconds or below), for example in trading, market making, exchanges or payments, and knowing where the time goes: runtime, memory, network and storage.

  • Strong production experience in at least one of TypeScript/Node.js, Rust, Java/Kotlin or Go.

  • Track record of design documents adopted beyond your own team.

Nice to have

  • Crypto experience: bridges, AMMs, exchange APIs, custody and key management, cross-chain settlement, solvers or intents.

  • Smart contracts for liquidity pools (Solidity).

  • Experience moving systems onto separate infrastructure with their own accounts, keys and access.

Location and hours

  • Remote, with at least three hours of overlap with 08:00–17:00 UTC.

  • The Liquidity team works with global exchanges whose eligibility rules exclude some jurisdictions, including the United States and Canada. We can only consider candidates located outside those jurisdictions.

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary

  • Equity package

  • Comprehensive health benefits

  • Unlimited PTO policy with encouraged minimum

  • Remote-first culture with emphasis on collaboration, communication, and flexibility

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s Financial Systems organization builds the technology that enables Stripe’s Finance org to operate accurately, efficiently, and at Stripe’s scale. We develop trusted data products, internal platforms and products, and intelligent workflows that help Finance teams manage complex global operations while maintaining strong controls.

This role will join a product team focused on transforming finance operations. You will initially work closely with Stripe’s tax and treasury organizations with opportunities for future impact in other parts of the Finance org. The products you build will help experts find trusted information, coordinate work, identify exceptions, and make timely decisions without stitching together context and workflows across multiple systems.

What you’ll do

You will develop products that will enable Stripe to maintain a continuously updated understanding of financial performance, automate complex operations while maintaining rigorous financial controls that minimize risk, and reduce toil for domain experts to free them for higher-value work. You will develop a deep understanding of expert users and their workflows, own the product strategy, turn it into a focused roadmap, and lead products from discovery through adoption and continuous improvement. The transformation your products enable will reduce risk, improve efficiency, automate manual tasks, and better enable Stripe to make timely financial decisions, deliver on regulatory commitments, and run a global-scale business.

This role combines internal product development, data platforms, automated workflow design, and applied AI. You will help develop purpose-built solutions, platforms, and autonomous agentic capabilities that reason over governed data, drive end-to-end workflows, and support expert decisions. Success requires understanding the capabilities and limitations of AI and machine learning when applied to business-critical, regulated, and strictly governed problems. You will also use AI-enabled tools throughout the product development lifecycle to accelerate discovery, prototyping, requirements development, evaluation, and iteration without compromising quality or controls.

Responsibilities

  • Develop a deep understanding of Finance users, jobs-to-be-done, compliance and regulatory considerations, and data dependencies, then translate that understanding into a clear roadmap for agentic automations.
  • Own products end to end, from problem discovery and strategy through delivery, adoption, measurement, and iteration
  • Build reusable data and self-serve workflow capabilities that eliminate manual overhead and enable future automated Finance use cases
  • Partner with Finance, engineering, data, security, legal, and others to make sound product and architecture tradeoffs in a business-critical and control-sensitive environment
  • Define measures to understand adoption, engagement, and impact for products and develop insights into the metrics to guide improvements to the product
  • Develop Finance products that enable Stripes to self-serve the creation and operation of agentic automations, while establishing appropriate boundaries for autonomous execution, evaluation methods, and controls for human review
  • Use AI-enabled tools throughout product development and help establish effective practices for AI-assisted discovery, prototyping, specification, testing, and iteration
  • Balance new product development with reliability, operational ownership, and the long-term health of the portfolio

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of product management or equivalent experience leading the development of complex software products
  • Experience independently taking a product from problem discovery through launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration
  • Experience working closely with engineering and data teams on systems involving data models, integrations, APIs, or complex operational workflows
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize the needs of multiple user groups and lead decisions across organizational boundaries
  • Ability to communicate clearly about product strategy, priorities, tradeoffs, risks, and results with both technical and nontechnical partners

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building products for tax, treasury, accounting, regulatory reporting, or other control-sensitive domains
  • Experience with enterprise data platforms, workflow systems, internal tool development, or systems of record
  • Experience applying AI or automation to expert workflows while preserving human review, auditability, and accountability
  • Experience maturing a product from active development into a reliable, sustainable operating model

Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

BUILT DIFFERENT

We believe there's a better way to build. One that moves faster, thinks bigger, and gives people the ownership to challenge what's been done before. We're not here to follow the standard. We're here to set a new one. We don't believe the best work happens inside rigid boxes. People are given real ownership, real responsibility, and the space to operate beyond a title. Scope grows with impact. Responsibility grows with trust. And the people who step up help shape what comes next. We're building an organization around ownership, not hierarchy, where your influence is defined by what you take on, not what's written on your email signature.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Superintendent, Mechanical leads mechanical and cooling systems field execution for a new data center build, owning day-to-day site operations for this scope in a high-stakes, mission-critical environment. Reporting to the Construction Manager and Director, Construction, this role drives schedule, coordinates mechanical trade partners, and enforces safety and quality from mobilization through turnover. Superintendents are the standard on a Hut 8 site: what you walk past, you approve.

Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Mechanical & Cooling Systems

Supervise installation of chilled water plants, air and liquid cooling systems, CRAHs, CDUs, heat exchangers, pumps, piping, valves, and insulation. Ensure mechanical systems are installed in accordance with design specifications, manufacturer requirements, and project quality standards.

Piping, Testing & System Cleanliness

Oversee hydronic piping installation, pressure testing, pipe flushing, chemical treatment, and system cleanliness protocols. Enforce strict quality standards for critical cooling loops, ensuring systems are ready for commissioning without contamination or installation deficiencies.

Trade Coordination & Sequencing

Own mechanical trade sequencing and manpower coordination across mechanical rooms, equipment yards, white space, and utility areas. Coordinate closely with electrical, plumbing, and controls teams to manage installation interfaces, resolve field conflicts, and maintain construction progress. Leverage BIM-supported coordination to identify and resolve clashes before installation.

Commissioning Handoff

Drive completion of mechanical installation checklists, equipment startup requirements, testing, adjusting, and balancing (TAB), and prerequisites supporting Level 1-3 commissioning. Support commissioning execution through Levels 4-5 alongside the CXQC Field Manager, ensuring mechanical systems are ready for integrated testing and turnover.

Safety & Quality Enforcement

Enforce mechanical construction safety standards, including rigging and lifting operations, hot work, confined space entry, pressure testing, and LOTO procedures. Hold mechanical trade partners accountable for first-time quality, documented inspections, and compliance with project specifications.

Planning, Documentation & Issues

Own the mechanical three-week look-ahead, daily coordination, manpower planning, and progress reporting. Drive mechanical RFIs and field issues to closure with the Project Engineer and discipline engineers. Maintain accurate QC records, test documentation, equipment startup reports, and as-built drawings.

ABOUT YOU

What we’re looking for:

  • 3+ years supervising mechanical construction trades on data center, semiconductor, hospital, or heavy industrial projects; mission-critical experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong technical knowledge of chilled water plants, HVAC systems, liquid cooling infrastructure, CRAHs, CDUs, pumps, heat exchangers, and hydronic piping systems.
  • Experience overseeing mechanical equipment installation, system startup, pressure testing, pipe flushing, hydronic balancing, and cleanliness requirements.
  • Experience supporting Level 1-5 commissioning activities, including mechanical system readiness, functional testing, and turnover documentation.
  • Strong trade-sequencing instincts in congested, schedule-critical environments; fluent in look-ahead planning and manpower loading.
  • Proven safety leadership across mechanical construction activities, including rigging, hot work, LOTO, and pressure testing; OSHA 30 preferred.
  • Ability to interpret mechanical drawings, P&IDs, equipment submittals, and coordinated BIM models.
  • Comfortable with Procore/ACC, BIM field use, and mechanical construction documentation.
  • Clear documentation habits, including daily reports, QC inspections, test

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Government Relations & Public Affairs team represents Stripe to governments, regulators, industry partners, and broader stakeholder audiences. We help policymakers understand the businesses building on Stripe, and help Stripe understand the policy decisions that affect them. Our EU work sits at the intersection of financial services, technology and economic policy. The team works closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Communications and regional product and go-to-market teams to translate Stripe’s experience and our users’ needs into effective policy engagement.

What you’ll do

We are looking for an EU Government Relations Manager to advance Stripe’s priorities in Brussels through effective advocacy and strong relationships with policymakers. You will bring deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy, and use that expertise to influence EU legislative and regulatory debates that matter to Stripe and the businesses we serve.

This is an advocacy-led role: you will develop and execute engagement strategies, build relationships across the EU institutions, and make persuasive arguments for policies that help European businesses start, grow and compete. Working closely with Policy Strategy, Legal and business colleagues, you will turn Stripe’s policy positions into practical advocacy, exercising judgment about where, when and how to engage.

The position is based in Brussels and reports to the Head of EU Government Relations. Its primary focus is the EU, working closely with colleagues across EMEA and globally.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute EU advocacy strategies for an agreed portfolio of issues, setting clear objectives, identifying opportunities to shape the policy making process.
  • Build and maintain relationships across the EU institutions, developing a strong network of policymakers, officials and advisers.
  • Represent Stripe directly in policy discussions, making clear, persuasive arguments grounded in our business, our users’ experiences and the needs of Europe’s digital economy.  
  • Bring deep subject expertise to Stripe’s advocacy in either payments and financial services or technology policy, while building the knowledge needed to engage effectively across a broad waterfront of issues.
  • Work closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Product and Go-To-Market colleagues to develop and refine advocacy positions, drawing on their expertise and ensuring our engagement reflects commercial and technical realities, and the needs of our users.
  • Build support for shared policy objectives through trade associations, industry coalitions and engagement with other companies and stakeholders.
  • Gather political and regulatory intelligence to guide advocacy decisions, keeping colleagues informed of material developments and recommending when and how Stripe should act.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in government relations, advocacy, public affairs or public policy, including direct experience of EU policymaking and engagement.
  • Deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy. Expertise in both is not required.
  • A demonstrated track record of developing and delivering advocacy strategies and influencing legislative or regulatory debates.
  • Strong understanding of EU institutions, political dynamics and legislative processes, with experience building productive relationships with policymakers and officials.

Multi-Site Construction Leadership

  • Portfolio Delivery: Lead construction of multiple concurrent AI data center builds, from site diligence and design through energization, commissioning, and ready-for-service (RFS).

Pre-Construction, Design & Power

  • Design Reviews: Lead multidisciplinary reviews of civil, structural, architectural, electrical, and mechanical design packages to resolve constructability, cost, and schedule issues before they reach the field.

AI & High-Density Infrastructure

  • Liquid Cooling: Deliver direct-to-chip liquid cooling and high-density power distribution for GPU/AI workloads.

  • Budget & EAC: Own site budgets, Estimate at Completion (EAC) forecasts, owner’s contingency, and value engineering across the portfolio.

  • Public-Sector & Permitting: Experience working with jurisdictions, inspectors, and building codes; military or public-sector engineering experience is a plus.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
 
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
 
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions.
 
Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out.
 
You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries.
  • Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline.
  • Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release.
  • Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision.
  • Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers.
  • Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product.
  • Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team.
  • Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads.
  • Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You  

  • 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team.
  • Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required.
  • Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output.
  • Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting.
  • Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus.
  • Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle.
  • Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee.
  • Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting.
  • Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale.
  • Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.
  • Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit.
  • A CPA, chartered tax adviser, or equivalent; or a degree in data science, computer science, or accounting.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI is building the infrastructure for stablecoin-based card issuance - bringing programmable, dollar-denominated value directly into everyday spend. This role will own one of our most consequential product lines: the card program that turns our rails into a spendable, real-world experience for institutions and their end users.

 

You'll work at the intersection of issuing banks, card networks, processors, and compliance to launch and run a program that doesn't have a playbook yet — because stablecoin-native card issuance is still being invented. You own the full P&L for the program - revenue, interchange economics, partner costs, and margin. You'll be the person who owns it end to end, from partner selection to program mechanics to day-to-day performance, reporting directly to the founders.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own the full P&L for the stablecoin card program: interchange revenue, network and processing costs, FX/conversion spread, and program margin

  • Serve as the primary owner of the card program's relationship with network partners (Visa, Mastercard) and issuing/sponsor banks, managing principal membership requirements and settlement operations

  • Lead card program launches end-to-end - program design, network approval, compliance sign-off, and go-live - across new markets and jurisdictions

  • Own the mechanics of stablecoin-to-fiat settlement for card transactions, working with Engineering to ensure authorization, clearing, and settlement run reliably across supported chains

  • Design and manage program features: credit vs. prepaid structures, spend limits, rewards, and fee models that drive usage and revenue

  • Partner with Compliance to maintain PCI DSS and network compliance standards, and to manage fraud, disputes, and chargebacks

  • Monitor program health daily - transaction volume, approval rates, fraud/loss rates, and unit economics - and report performance to founders

  • Act as the internal and external expert on the program, representing it in partner negotiations, network reviews, and customer-facing conversations

  • Continuously evaluate new networks, chains, and settlement rails to expand where and how the program can operate

 

You might be a fit if

  • 5+ years of experience in card issuing, card program management, or payments, ideally with direct exposure to Visa/Mastercard program mechanics

  • Track record of owning a card program's P&L — not just operating it, but improving its unit economics

  • Deep familiarity with card network rules, issuing bank/BIN sponsor relationships, and settlement operations

  • Comfortable working at the intersection of stablecoins and traditional card rails, even if you're newer to crypto specifically

  • Strong instincts for compliance and risk — you know how to move fast without cutting corners on fraud, disputes, or regulatory requirements

  • Can operate independently and drive a program forward without a playbook to follow

  • You want real ownership over a P&L, not just a seat at the table

 

Why This Role Matters

Card issuance is where stablecoins meet the real world - the moment programmable dollars become something people can actually spend. This role owns that moment for HIFI. You'll build and run the program that turns our infrastructure into a product people use every day, with direct ownership over how it performs financially.

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.
